title: API requires either TWS or IB Gateway connection
claim: API connection must route through either the TWS application (with GUI) or the IB Gateway (headless). Direct socket connection requires one of these intermediaries.
support: The book explicitly states 'The API allows you to connect through either the TWS or the IB Gateway' and describes both connection methods as the only available options.
mechanism: TWS and IB Gateway act as intermediary services between API client and IB's backend trading system.
assumptions: TWS/Gateway are running and reachable on the network
failure_modes: API client cannot connect if both TWS and Gateway are down
Network failure between client and intermediary breaks connection
validation: Attempt API connection without TWS/Gateway running; confirm connection fails

title: API Order IDs must be strictly increasing
claim: When placing new orders via API, each order ID must be greater than the previously used order ID. Resubmitting with the same order ID modifies an existing order.
support: The book states: 'When you place a new order using the API, the order id number must be greater than the previously used numbers' and 'if you place an order with an Order ID of 11, the next order you place should have an Order ID of at least 12'.
mechanism: API client maintains order ID counter; IB Gateway/TWS uses order ID to distinguish new vs. modified orders.
assumptions: Order ID counter persists across API sessions (needs verification for modern IB API)
No order ID wraparound or reset mechanism documented
failure_modes: Attempting to place new order with ID <= last used ID may fail silently or modify existing order
Order ID counter exhaustion (if 32-bit signed int used, max ~2B orders)
validation: Send two new orders with decreasing IDs; verify second order fails or modifies first order

title: IB Gateway enables GUI-less production deployment
claim: IB Gateway allows API trading without a running TWS GUI application, reducing memory/CPU overhead and enabling true headless server deployment.

source.section: Run the API through the IB Gateway

support: The book states 'Connecting through the IB Gateway allows you to use the API without a large GUI application running' and recommends using Gateway in production after testing via TWS.
mechanism: IB Gateway is a lightweight background service; no GUI means less resource consumption and fewer crash modes.
assumptions: IB Gateway and TWS have equivalent API feature support (needs verification)
failure_modes: Gateway crashes leave no GUI for debugging unlike TWS
Differences in order routing or data delivery between TWS and Gateway not fully documented
validation: Deploy API via IB Gateway and confirm order placement, fills, and account updates work identically to TWS

title: API connection can bypass TWS precautionary checks
claim: TWS has optional precautionary checks (e.g., order size limits, price reasonableness); API orders can be configured to ignore these checks via a TWS setting.

source.section: API Orders and TWS Precautionary Settings

support: The book documents a TWS setting 'Bypass Order Precautions for API Orders' that, when enabled in IB Gateway, causes all API orders to ignore user-set precautionary settings.
mechanism: TWS maintains configurable safety filters; API can request exemption from these filters.
assumptions: Precautionary checks include price reasonableness, order size, daily loss limits, etc. (not fully enumerated)
Bypass setting is per-API-session or per-account
failure_modes: Traders can accidentally place erroneous orders if bypass is enabled
Market conditions or exchange rules may reject bypassed orders anyway, leading to unexpected failures
validation: Place order with extreme price or size with bypass disabled, then enabled; verify acceptance/rejection differences

title: Order modification via same order ID
claim: To modify an existing order, resubmit using the same order ID with updated price or quantity. Order type and action (buy/sell) cannot be changed; requires cancellation and new order.
support: The book provides a 'Modified Order Example' showing order ID 3 submitted twice: once with limit $85.25, then with limit $86.25, demonstrating that price can be updated via same ID.
mechanism: API gateway uses order ID as unique identifier; duplicate ID triggers update instead of insert.
assumptions: Only price and quantity can be modified; order type, action, time-in-force cannot be modified
Modification replaces entire order record or patches specific fields (not fully clear)
failure_modes: Modifying unsupported field may fail silently or be ignored
Race condition if order fills between modification check and resubmission
validation: Submit order ID 1 with price P1; modify to price P2; verify order ID 1 is updated, not duplicated

title: Account Available Funds calculated from Equity with Loan Value and Initial Margin
claim: For securities accounts: Available Funds = Equity with Loan Value - Initial Margin. For commodities: Available Funds = Net Liquidation Value - Initial Margin.
support: The book defines Available Funds for both securities and commodities in the Account Page Values reference table.
mechanism: Available Funds is a derived metric; represents capital available for new positions without violating margin requirements.
assumptions: Initial Margin is the overnight margin requirement, not current intraday margin
Equity with Loan Value includes margin loan value at current market prices
Calculation is real-time updated
failure_modes: Margin call if Available Funds goes negative (not explicitly documented)
Intraday initial margin changes may not be reflected immediately
validation: Query account Available Funds; compute manually from reported Equity with Loan Value and Initial Margin; verify match

title: Buying Power for margin accounts is 4x Available Funds
claim: For standard margin accounts: Buying Power = Available Funds × 4. For cash accounts: Buying Power = minimum(current Equity with Loan Value, previous day Equity with Loan Value) - Initial Margin.
support: The Account Page Values table defines Buying Power separately for cash and margin account types with explicit formulas.
mechanism: Margin accounts can borrow 4:1 against available funds (standard Reg T requirement in US); cash accounts have no leverage.
assumptions: 4:1 ratio is Reg T requirement and has not changed since 2015
Buying Power calculation uses same-day or next-opening prices
Account type (cash vs. margin) is correctly flagged in IB system
failure_modes: Buying power may be further constrained by broker risk limits or account-level restrictions
Intraday vs. overnight buying power may differ
International margin requirements may differ
validation: Query account type (cash vs. margin), Available Funds, and Buying Power; verify 4x relationship for margin

title: Day Trades Remaining counter tracks pattern-day-trader restrictions
claim: Field Day Trades Remaining shows the number of day trades left within a rolling pattern-day-trader period. Additional fields Day Trades Remaining T+1/T+2/T+3/T+4 track rolling 4-day windows.
support: The Account Page Values table lists both 'Day Trades Remaining' and 'Day Trades Remaining T+1, T+2, T+3, T+4' as distinct fields with brief descriptions.
mechanism: Regulatory pattern-day-trader rule limits cash accounts and low-balance margin accounts to 3-4 day trades per 5-day period.
assumptions: Day trade counting rules are correctly implemented by IB
T+1/T+2/T+3/T+4 fields represent rolling windows (T = today)
Reset timing is end-of-day or end-of-week (not fully specified)
failure_modes: Counter may lag real trades by hours; order may be rejected if near limit
Definition of 'day trade' may not align with trader expectations (e.g., buy/sell same security same day)
validation: Execute 3 day trades; verify Day Trades Remaining decreases; attempt 4th day trade and verify rejection

title: Margin cushion is calculated as Excess Liquidity
claim: Field Cushion shows current margin cushion; defined in another field as Excess Liquidity = Equity with Loan Value - Maintenance Margin.
support: The Account Page Values table defines both 'Cushion' and 'Excess Liquidity' as distinct fields, with Excess Liquidity providing the explicit formula.
mechanism: Cushion is margin buffer; when Excess Liquidity < 0, account is in margin call.
assumptions: Maintenance Margin is the minimum margin requirement to hold positions (lower than initial margin)
Real-time market prices are used in calculation
failure_modes: Market gap can cause cushion to go negative overnight, triggering margin call
Maintenance margin changes intraday with market volatility or position changes
validation: Query Cushion and Excess Liquidity; verify they are identical; calculate as (Equity with Loan Value - Maintenance Margin)

title: Leverage defined as Gross Position Value / Net Liquidation Value for securities
claim: For securities: Leverage = Gross Position Value / Net Liquidation Value. Represents the multiple of account equity deployed as gross notional position.
support: The Account Page Values table explicitly defines Leverage for securities with this formula.
mechanism: Leverage metric quantifies how much notional exposure is taken relative to account equity.
assumptions: Gross Position Value includes both long and short positions as positive values (not net)
Net Liquidation Value is account equity at current market prices
Leverage is real-time and changes with every market tick
failure_modes: High leverage (e.g., > 10x) may trigger broker risk limits or margin calls
Leverage can spike unexpectedly on market gaps
validation: Query Leverage, Gross Position Value, Net Liquidation Value; verify formula

title: Order margin and commission impact available pre-trade via whatIf flag
claim: ActiveX/C++/Java API orders support a whatIf() field; when set to true, the order is not sent but margin and commission data is returned via the OrderState callback without actual execution.
support: The ActiveX Order Attributes table lists 'whatIf() As Integer' with description: 'Use to request pre-trade commissions and margin information. If set to true, margin and commissions data is received back via the OrderState() object for the openOrder() callback.'
mechanism: Pre-trade validation order type allows simulation of order impact without sending to market.
assumptions: whatIf flag returns accurate commissions and margin for the order
OrderState object is populated with margin and commission fields
whatIf orders do not consume order IDs or affect any account state
failure_modes: whatIf response may not reflect market conditions at true execution time
Commissions may differ from quoted amount if order partially fills
validation: Send order with whatIf=true; verify order is not executed; confirm OrderState contains commission and margin fields

title: Order commission and margin fields in OrderState callback
claim: The IOrderState object returned via openOrder() callback includes fields: commission, commissionCurrency, equityWithLoan, initMargin, maintMargin, maxCommission, minCommission.
support: The IOrderState table lists these commission and margin fields with brief descriptions of each.
mechanism: Each order state update includes full account impact snapshot.
assumptions: Fields are populated for all orders, not just whatIf orders
Commission range (min/max) reflects uncertainty in partial fill scenarios
equityWithLoan and margin fields are cumulative or snapshot at order submission time
failure_modes: Real execution commissions may differ from min/max range
equityWithLoan field may not reflect subsequent orders in flight
validation: Place order and inspect OrderState callback; verify all commission/margin fields populated

title: Modern IB API likely uses C++/Java instead of ActiveX/DDE
claim: The book extensively documents DDE (Excel) and ActiveX APIs, but modern interactive brokers API likely emphasizes WebSocket or direct socket C++/Java bindings, with DDE/ActiveX deprecated.
support: The 2015 manual dedicates ~40% of content to DDE (Excel-based) and ActiveX; modern trading systems typically avoid COM and Excel-based APIs.
mechanism: Technology shift from COM (Windows-centric, high latency) to modern WebSocket/socket APIs (cross-platform, lower latency).
assumptions: IB has modernized its API offerings since 2015
Legacy DDE/ActiveX still supported but not recommended for new development
failure_modes: Extracting DDE/ActiveX specs may lead to outdated implementation assumptions
validation: Check current Interactive Brokers API documentation; identify DDE/ActiveX deprecation status

title: Account margin rules likely changed post-2008; regulatory framework not covered
claim: The 2015 manual does not explicitly address post-2008 regulatory changes (Dodd-Frank, Volcker Rule, MiFID II) or non-US regulatory frameworks; margin and risk rules may have evolved significantly.
support: The manual is a technical reference for IB APIs/account structure; no section on regulatory compliance or international rules.
mechanism: Regulatory environment post-2008 imposed new constraints on leverage, position limits, reporting, and risk controls.
assumptions: IB has adapted its systems to comply with modern regulations
This manual predates or omits regulatory commentary
failure_modes: System designed to 2015 margin model may violate modern regulations
Cross-asset or cross-jurisdictional trading may have undocumented constraints not reflected in this manual
validation: Compare 2015 margin rules to current IB documentation; identify regulatory changes
